quests.sentence: Honestly? I'd already made up my mind before you even finished the sentence.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had made up (shortened to 'd made up) is the past perfect form, showing this happened before another past event.
quests.nativeTip: The decision was made before the other person even finished speaking, an earlier point.
quests.example: Honestly? I'd already made up my mind before you even finished the sentence.

quests.sentence: You made a fair point, though.
quests.ruleExplanation: Made is the simple past form, describing a completed past action.
quests.nativeTip: This is a simple completed observation about something already said.
quests.example: You made a fair point, though.

quests.sentence: Give it a minute — I'll come around.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will come around is the will-future form, describing a decision made in the moment.
quests.nativeTip: This is a decision or promise being made right now, in response to the conversation.
quests.example: Give it a minute — I'll come around.

quests.sentence: Morale's been low for a while, and it's starting to show in the numbers.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has been (shortened to 's been) is the present perfect form, describing a situation continuing up to the present.
quests.nativeTip: Focus on the first half — a situation that began in the past and is still true now.
quests.example: Morale's been low for a while, and it's starting to show in the numbers.

quests.sentence: Turnover doubled compared to this time last year.
quests.ruleExplanation: Doubled is the simple past form, describing a completed change measured against a past reference point.
quests.nativeTip: This compares a specific past period to a finished point in time.
quests.example: Turnover doubled compared to this time last year.

quests.conceptTitle: Timeline Mapping: Simple Present (Future Time Clause)
quests.sentence: Something has to change before this situation gets any worse.
quests.ruleExplanation: Gets is the simple present form used for future meaning inside a time clause beginning with before.
quests.nativeTip: The worsening is still ahead, but notice the verb form right after 'before'.
quests.example: Something has to change before this situation gets any worse.

quests.sentence: They hadn't spoken in years, not since the wedding.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hadn't spoken is the negative past perfect form, describing a long-continuing situation before a later past reference point.
quests.nativeTip: This long silence is measured from an earlier point, up to the moment being described.
quests.example: They hadn't spoken in years, not since the wedding.

quests.sentence: Their mother's funeral was the first time they'd been in the same room since.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had been (shortened to 'd been) is the past perfect form, describing a state true up until a specific later past event.
quests.nativeTip: This describes their situation up to that later past event, the funeral.
quests.example: Their mother's funeral was the first time they'd been in the same room since.

quests.sentence: Whether they'll patch things up now remains to be seen.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will patch up is the will-future form, describing an uncertain future outcome.
quests.nativeTip: This is an open question about what will happen going forward.
quests.example: Whether they'll patch things up now remains to be seen.

quests.sentence: The draft reads fine on its own, but it hasn't earned that ending yet.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hasn't earned is the negative present perfect form, describing something not yet accomplished up to the present.
quests.nativeTip: This describes something still missing, as of right now.
quests.example: The draft reads fine on its own, but it hasn't earned that ending yet.

quests.sentence: Earlier versions tried something bolder and frankly worked better.
quests.ruleExplanation: Tried and worked are simple past forms, describing completed past attempts.
quests.nativeTip: This compares finished, earlier attempts, all in the past.
quests.example: Earlier versions tried something bolder and frankly worked better.

quests.sentence: Readers will forgive a lot if the characters feel real.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will forgive is the will-future form, describing a predicted future reaction.
quests.nativeTip: This predicts a general future reaction based on a condition.
quests.example: Readers will forgive a lot if the characters feel real.

quests.sentence: Confidence hasn't fully recovered since the last downturn.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hasn't recovered is the negative present perfect form, describing a situation continuing from a past point to now.
quests.nativeTip: This situation began in the past and continues to be true now.
quests.example: Confidence hasn't fully recovered since the last downturn.

quests.sentence: Analysts had underestimated the speed of the rebound.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had underestimated is the past perfect form, describing an earlier misjudgment relative to a later point in the story.
quests.nativeTip: This mistaken expectation is placed before a later point being discussed.
quests.example: Analysts had underestimated the speed of the rebound.

quests.sentence: By most accounts, growth will have slowed considerably by year's end.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will have slowed is the future perfect form, describing a change expected to be complete by a future point.
quests.nativeTip: Year's end is the future point by which this change is expected to be complete.
quests.example: By most accounts, growth will have slowed considerably by year's end.

quests.sentence: Nobody had given this team a real shot before the season started.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had given is the past perfect form, describing a situation true before another past event.
quests.nativeTip: This lack of belief existed before an even earlier reference point, the season's start.
quests.example: Nobody had given this team a real shot before the season started.

quests.sentence: They proved everyone wrong, one upset at a time.
quests.ruleExplanation: Proved is the simple past form, describing the central completed action of the story.
quests.nativeTip: This is the main storyline, told as a completed sequence.
quests.example: They proved everyone wrong, one upset at a time.

quests.sentence: History will remember this run long after the trophy's been forgotten.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will remember is the will-future form, describing a long-term future prediction.
quests.nativeTip: This is a prediction about the distant future.
quests.example: History will remember this run long after the trophy's been forgotten.

quests.sentence: The treatment hadn't been tested on this age group before this trial.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hadn't been tested is the negative past perfect form, describing a situation true before a later past event.
quests.nativeTip: This gap existed before the trial being described, an earlier point.
quests.example: The treatment hadn't been tested on this age group before this trial.

quests.sentence: Early results showed a marked improvement within weeks.
quests.ruleExplanation: Showed is the simple past form, describing a completed research result.
quests.nativeTip: This reports a completed finding from the trial.
quests.example: Early results showed a marked improvement within weeks.

quests.sentence: If the trend holds, the therapy will have reached full approval within two years.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will have reached is the future perfect form, describing an outcome expected to be complete by a future point.
quests.nativeTip: Two years from now is the point by which this outcome is expected.
quests.example: If the trend holds, the therapy will have reached full approval within two years.

quests.sentence: I hadn't realized how much I'd changed until I saw those old photos.
quests.ruleExplanation: Hadn't realized is the negative past perfect form, describing a state true before a later past realization.
quests.nativeTip: This lack of awareness existed before an even earlier change had already taken place.
quests.example: I hadn't realized how much I'd changed until I saw those old photos.

quests.sentence: Something in me had already let go, long before I admitted it.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had let go is the past perfect form, describing a change that occurred before a later past event.
quests.nativeTip: The inner change happened well before the moment of admitting it.
quests.example: Something in me had already let go, long before I admitted it.

quests.sentence: From here, I'm just going to see where it leads.
quests.ruleExplanation: Am going to see uses going to for an intention already decided, going forward from now.
quests.nativeTip: This describes an intention already settled on, going forward.
quests.example: From here, I'm just going to see where it leads.

quests.sentence: By the time anyone thought to check on him, he'd been gone for hours.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had been gone (shortened to 'd been gone) is the past perfect form, describing a state true before a later past event.
quests.nativeTip: His absence had already lasted for a while before anyone checked, an earlier situation.
quests.example: By the time anyone thought to check on him, he'd been gone for hours.

quests.sentence: The note he left explained everything, in the end.
quests.ruleExplanation: Explained is the simple past form, describing the resolving action of the narrative.
quests.nativeTip: This is the resolving event of the story, told as a completed action.
quests.example: The note he left explained everything, in the end.

quests.sentence: Whatever comes next, they'll figure it out together.
quests.ruleExplanation: Will figure out is the will-future form, describing a confident prediction about the future.
quests.nativeTip: This expresses confidence about handling something in the future.
quests.example: Whatever comes next, they'll figure it out together.

quests.sentence: She'd spent the better part of a decade proving people wrong, and she wasn't about to stop now.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had spent (shortened to 'd spent) is the past perfect form, describing a long effort true up until a later past point.
quests.nativeTip: This long effort is measured up to a later point being described in the story.
quests.example: She'd spent the better part of a decade proving people wrong, and she wasn't about to stop now.

quests.sentence: The doubters had gone quiet a long time before the trophy ever showed up.
quests.ruleExplanation: Had gone quiet is the past perfect form, describing a change that occurred before a later past event.
quests.nativeTip: This change happened well before the later past event, the trophy's arrival.
quests.example: The doubters had gone quiet a long time before the trophy ever showed up.

quests.sentence: Whatever comes next, she's already won more than most people ever will.
quests.ruleExplanation: Has already won is the present perfect form, describing an accomplishment that remains true in the present, regardless of what the future holds.
quests.nativeTip: Focus on the middle of the sentence — an achievement that's already true and still stands, right now.
quests.example: Whatever comes next, she's already won more than most people ever will.
